title: Record the characteristic polynomial of one 48-dimensional eigenspace of s
body:
## Change and mathematical scope

Finite exact computation for one invariant subspace of the historical `c=1` one-slot block. No new kappa. The selected conditional kappa stays `781451/250000000`.

Let `s = (0 4 3 7)(5 6)` with all signs `+1`. On the moved sign character `eps[1] * eps[2]`, the eigenvalue-`+1` eigenspace of `s` is 48-dimensional. The monic characteristic polynomial of `A_1` on that space is

```text
x^10 (x-2)^6 (x+2)^6
  (x^5 - 4x^4 - 24x^3 + 80x^2 + 80x - 160)
  (x^5 + 4x^4 - 24x^3 - 80x^2 + 80x + 160)
  (x^8 - 4x^7 - 72x^6 + 240x^5 + 784x^4 - 2208x^3 + 1920x - 768)
  (x^8 + 4x^7 - 72x^6 - 240x^5 + 784x^4 + 2208x^3 - 1920x - 768)
```

Ascending-coefficient SHA256 of `chi_{A_1}` is `1230f7227b6cbd0ad1383273a601bb4f517462ca663235c673e6b6bb13f1b3af`. The eigenvalue-`-1` space of the same character is isospectral. The other character preserved by this `s`, `eps[5] * eps[6]`, has a different degree-48 polynomial, recorded in `research/c1-moved-48-charpoly/PROOF.md`.

Every irreducible factor of the corresponding integer polynomial `chi_B` divides a published `c=1` sector factor of the degree-881 one-slot minimal polynomial. The comparison reads those coefficients. It does not replay that certificate.

This is a proof by exact linear algebra of one characteristic polynomial. It is not a minimal polynomial of the full operator, not an eigenvalue-`i` computation, and not a census of every invariant subspace. The polynomial is not square-free. Algebraic multiplicity of eigenvalue 0 is 10. That does not give the geometric multiplicity, and it does not exhibit a signed permutation outside the centralizer of `s`.

## Task and overlap

Base commit `17469fff78c22941280f04d39dc5a1faee09c840`. The diff is only `research/c1-moved-48-charpoly/`.

Task card `formal-interface-lemma`. Scope status: **changed**. The card asks for a formal caller binding. [PR #7009](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/7009) leaves open the characteristic polynomial of one 48-dimensional eigenspace of `s` on a moved 192-character. This package answers that question for the real eigenvalue `+1` on `eps[1] * eps[2]`. It does not add a Lean binding and does not recompute the 216-dimensional polynomial of merged PR #6964.

The query is the frozen interface used by `research/centre-polynomial-cache-limits/`, SHA256 `5c6c51fbffc07a683e922f17532fd90262ae9e23cc3560a696002073dd234ef3`.

Local overlap on 2026-11-10 covered 10178 of 10178 HEAD notes and found no match for `48-dimensional eigenspace` or `moved 192`. A GitHub search of open pull requests and discussions for `48-dimensional eigenspace` returned only PR #7009. The offline overlap cache had no usable remote snapshot. Closed PRs were searched through local READMEs, task metadata, and the ledger only.

## Validation

CPython 3.12.3, standard library only. Both registered modes passed:

```sh
python3 -B scripts/research_package.py --package research/c1-moved-48-charpoly
```

Marker `PASS_C1_MOVED_48_CHARPOLY`. Metadata check: `PASS_PACKAGE_METADATA_AND_PINS`. Selected-baseline orientation: `PASS_RESEARCH_BASELINE_BINDINGS_ONLY`.

The verifier rebuilds the sign stabilizer, both characters, the four real 48-dimensional eigenspaces, and both integer matrices of `B = 4 A_1`. The canonical basis and matrix are pinned. Characteristic polynomials are lifted by the Chinese remainder theorem from the Hessenberg recurrence. Factors are checked by multiplication and by the Rabin irreducibility test. Rejection controls cover a coordinate transposition, a swapped port label, a character-sign flip, a one-entry matrix change, a dropped factor, and a sign error in a basis vector.

Not run: Lean, Docker, the degree-881 replay, the selected cold replay, an eigenvalue-`i` basis, and the exact rational nullity of the pinned matrix.

## Credit

JoyboyBrian recorded the open decomposition question in discussion comment 19144258. PR #7009, by unpaidmoon, recorded `s` and the multiplicity pattern `48^4` without a basis. The operators `g` and `t` come from the sign-stabilizer split, PR #6944. The polynomial method follows `research/a1-joint-216-charpoly/` (PR #6964) on a different subspace. Ali Romman's PR4958 and PR4720 retain the query and the Bell action. Nick Petalas's PR5120 is the degree-410 lower bound. Krzysztof Wojt's PR5168 is the degree-881 one-slot annihilator. The doubled representation comes from PR1719. New work is Apache-2.0.

Prepared by unpaidmoon with substantial Cursor Grok assistance. The assistant derived the basis and checked the polynomial. This is not an independent human or proof-kernel review.

## Open next questions

Recorded in `research/c1-moved-48-charpoly/TASK.json`.

- What is the characteristic polynomial, over `Q(i)`, of one eigenvalue-`i` eigenspace of `s` on `eps[1] * eps[2]`? The integer basis used here solves only the eigenvalues `±1`.
- What is the geometric multiplicity of eigenvalue 0 on this pinned 48-by-48 matrix? Algebraic multiplicity is 10. This is not the 216-by-216 matrix of PR #6964.
